en: Andres Bonifacio, not Jose Rizal, founded the secret revolutionary society called the Katipunan to fight Spanish colonizers.
The Philippines officially celebrates Independence Day on June 12 to commemorate the 1898 declaration by Emilio Aguinaldo.
The legislative branch, called Congress, is bicameral and consists of both the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Philippine Constitution strictly limits the President to a single six-year term without the possibility of re-election.
The Sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine, is the official national flower of the Philippines, not the Waling-waling orchid.
Filipino is the national language based on Tagalog but officially enriched with words from other Philippine and foreign languages.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño, not a local patron saint or a historical hero.
The Igorot indigenous groups primarily reside in the mountainous Cordillera Administrative Region of Luzon, not the southern island of Mindanao.
Lapu-Lapu was a native chieftain of Mactan in Cebu, not a Tagalog ruler from the island of Luzon.
Supreme Court justices are appointed by the President from a shortlist prepared by the Judicial and Bar Council, not elected by voters.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird of prey, not a mammal, despite its alternative name monkey-eating eagle.
Voting in Philippine national elections is a right and duty for all registered citizens who are at least eighteen years old.
